title: MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.3 (Logit-Level Formulation of Label Smoothing Loss), Section 3.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The printed formula 'L_LS ≈ α(z_gt − (1/K)Σ_k z_k) − log Σ_j e^{z_j}' contains a spurious log-sum-exp term. Direct derivation (and the paper's own Appendix B, eqs. 21–24) shows the LSE terms cancel exactly: H(s,q) = −(1−α)z_gt − (α/K)Σz_k + log(Σe^z), H(y,q) = −z_gt + log(Σe^z), hence L_LS = H(s,q) − H(y,q) = α(z_gt − (1/K)Σz_k) with no '−log Σe^z' term. The main-text theorem is therefore inconsistent with its own appendix proof, which derives the exact form without the extra term.

The text claims 'Logit Penalty occasionally displays increased d̄_within and R² values', but Table 2 shows Logit Penalty d̄_within = 0.284 (train) / 0.314 (val), both strictly BELOW Baseline (0.311 / 0.331); only R² exceeds baseline, and OLS/Zipf-LS also exceed baseline R². The sentence 'MaxSup maintains d̄_within reductions similar to other methods, suggesting only marginal benefits in preserving intra-class statistics' also contradicts the paper's central claim (abstract, Introduction, Figure 1) that MaxSup preserves/restores intra-class variation.

The table attributes 'Logit Normalization' to reference [3], but reference [3] is Chen et al., 'HSVA: Hierarchical semantic-visual adaptation for zero-shot learning' (NeurIPS 2021), which is unrelated to logit normalization. The logit-normalization work actually discussed in the text (Appendix H) is reference [38], Wei et al., 'Mitigating neural network overconfidence with logit normalization'. This is an attribution mismatch; the '[3*]' marker appears to be a typo for '[38*]'.

The Abstract claims MaxSup 'helps restore intra-class variation and sharpens inter-class boundaries' and hedges ('may contribute', 'likely plays a role', 'in certain settings'), while the Introduction states definitively that MaxSup 'alleviates severe intra-class collapse', 'sustains richer intra-class variability' and 'consistently boosts top-1 accuracy'. Section 4.1.1 then states MaxSup shows 'only marginal benefits in preserving intra-class statistics'. The central claimed benefit is directly undercut by the paper's own results section.
The sentence refers to 'Theorem 3.2', but the preceding result is 'Lemma 3.2' (Decomposition of Cross-Entropy Loss with Soft Labels). No Theorem 3.2 exists in the paper.
The overview cites 'Theorem 3.4, Equation (5)' for the regularization/error-amplification decomposition, but the actual result is 'Corollary 3.4' with Equation (5). No Theorem 3.4 exists.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix H, 'recent approaches that also identify and aim to fix the issues of Label Smoothing on misclassified samples [6, 38]' and 'these norm-based methods [6, 38, 4]'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [6] (Gao et al., 'Towards a better understanding of label smoothing in neural machine translation', ACL 2020) studies LS in NMT and is not a norm-based method nor a work that fixes LS overconfidence on misclassified samples. Citing it alongside [38] for these specific claims is questionable; the bibliographic cross-check does not support the attribution.

summary: Uncertainty-mode verification of 'MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing' (65 snippets triaged; 20 escalated for specialist review). One high-confidence mathematical error was confirmed: Theorem 3.3 prints an extra '−log Σ_j e^{z_j}' term in the logit-level Label Smoothing loss, which cancels exactly (as the paper's own Appendix B proof shows), making the main-text theorem inconsistent with its proof and requiring correction. Additional moderate-confidence findings: Section 4.1.1's analysis contradicts its own Table 2 (Logit Penalty d̄_within never increases) and undercuts the paper's central claim about intra-class variation; Table 13 misattributes 'Logit Normalization' to reference [3] instead of [38]; the Abstract/Introduction overstate MaxSup's intra-class benefit relative to Section 4.1.1; two misreferences (Theorem 3.2→Lemma 3.2; Theorem 3.4→Corollary 3.4); placeholder/template image artifacts where referenced figures should appear; a questionable citation of [6]; and an uncited reference [11]. The verified math (Lemma 3.2, Corollary 3.4, MaxSup equations 6–8, gradient analyses, Appendix proofs A and C) is internally consistent. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION.
